newsitem.title: BELGIUM: W. Europe chemical industry to grow 2.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: W. Europe chemical industry to grow 2.5 pct.

text.p: Volume growth in the western European chemical industry is forecast at 2.5 percent both in 1997 and 1998, up from two percent in 1996, the European Chemical Industry Council (CEFIC) said on Friday.
CEFIC also predicted export growth at five percent this year, up from 3.9 percent in 1996. The forecast includes intra-European trade.
"Trends in the west European chemical industry magnified those observed in manufacturing industry as a whole, with the recovery taking shape in the second half of 1996," CEFIC said in a statement.
However, even the more robust outlook for the industry would be insufficient to stabilise employment and further job restructuring was expected, albeit at a slower pace, CEFIC said.
Inventories were thought to have reached normal levels, both within the chemical industry itself and with its customers.
"Exports are performing well due to the strong U.S. dollar and to sustained overseas demand, especially from the USA and South-East Asia," it said.

Low interest rates and solid profits were likely to stimulate investment, CEFIC said. "However, investment will be geared mostly towards expansion of existing operations rather than greenfield developments," it added.
In terms of the individual sectors, plastics, organics, synthetic rubber and fibres are expected to be the most buoyant segments of the west European chemical industry this year.
"Growth in pharmaceuticals is expected to be more modest, largely as a result of government initiatives designed to check public spending."
CEFIC said that given the importance of export sales, its forecasts are particularly sensitive to fluctuations in exchange rates.
